title: The Wide Gate
paragraphs: Because deep down—you already feel it.

That quiet tension in your chest…
That whisper you try to ignore…
That moment when everyone is celebrating something, and your spirit feels uneasy.

Jesus said it without softening the blow:
“Enter through the narrow gate. For wide is the gate and broad is the road that leads to destruction, and many enter through it.” (Matthew 7:13)

Not a few.
Not the obvious villains.
Not just the “worst of the worst.”

The liked.
The trending.
The applauded.
The wide gate is crowded for a reason.

It tells you:
“Follow your heart.”
“Do what makes you happy.”
“Live your truth.”
But here’s the hard truth we don’t like to hear:
Your heart—apart from God—can lead you straight into destruction.
That’s what makes the wide road so dangerous.

It doesn’t feel like rebellion.
It feels like freedom.

It doesn’t look like darkness.
It looks like fun.

It doesn’t sound like lies.
It sounds like acceptance.
They cheer you on while you walk it.
He doesn’t shout to shame you.
Because on the other side of that wide gate is not life.

It’s loss.
It’s separation.
It’s eternal distance from the God who made you.
And here’s where it gets personal—

You can be surrounded by people…
and still be walking toward destruction.

You can be affirmed…
and still be far from truth.

You can be celebrated…
and still be spiritually lost.
That’s why Jesus offers something radically different:
Because the narrow gate demands something the wide gate never will:

You don’t walk through it carrying pride.
You don’t squeeze through it holding on to secret sin.
You don’t enter it while insisting, “My way is better.”

Not to destroy you—
but to free you.

Free from guilt.
Free from pretending.
Free from the exhausting lie that you are your own savior.
And here’s the Gospel—the part that changes everything:
The narrow gate is not a path you earn.
He didn’t stand far off and point the way.

He stepped into our broken road.
He lived the sinless life we couldn’t live.
He carried our sin—your sin—on the cross.

Every hidden thing.
Every compromise.
Every moment you chose the wide road.
Then He rose again—proving that sin doesn’t get the final word… and death doesn’t win.
So now the invitation is not: “Try harder.”

Turn from the road that is killing you.
Turn from the version of “freedom” that is actually bondage.
And walk toward the One who offers real life.

Not shallow happiness.
Not temporary highs.
You don’t need the crowd to validate your direction.
You need Christ to redeem it.
And maybe that’s why this stopped you today.
You’ve been walking with the crowd…
but thinking about the narrow gate.

Not tomorrow.
Not when you “fix yourself.”
Not when it’s more convenient.

The wide gate…
or the narrow way.
If this stirred something in you, don’t ignore it.
Because eternity is not a game.

And the gate you choose…
matters.
